title: Introduce invocation stability score and explainer sparkline
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: initial: fail (unit-test flaky on sparkline rendering) -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Adds a per-invocation stability score and small explainer sparkline in the Redwood Console. New metric and dashboard panels for correlating stability with token cost and KV-cache behavior. Backwards-compatible; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: We frequently triage noisy tail alerts where per-invocation behavior (latency spikes, cost bursts, fallback model use, cache misses) is hard to summarize. This PR introduces an 'invocation stability score' (0-100) that aggregates several per-invocation signals into a single explainable metric, and an inline explainer sparkline rendered in the Console that highlights the top three contributors for that invocation. Goals: 1) make long-tail instability actionable in triage and SLO dashboards, 2) provide compact visual explanation in the Console and alert payloads, 3) enable automated alert tuning by mapping stability to severity tiers.

What this changes: implemented a stability scoring pipeline and UI glue across three areas: metrics ingest, trace enrichment, and Console panels. The score is computed at ingestion time as a weighted combination of normalized features: phase_latency_variance, token_cost_zscore, kv_cache_miss_rate, model_fallback_flag, and response_size_skew. We persist score and top contributors as numeric tags on the invocation metric and as enriched span attributes for traces. On the Console side we add an "Invocation Stability" sparkline panel that embeds a small contributor bar for each sampled invocation and an expanded explainer modal showing raw signals and normalization details.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-8734) with scoring formula and normalization weights
- [x] Metrics pipeline: score computation and tag emission (observability/metrics/invocation_stability.go)
- [x] Tracing: span enrichment and attribute mapping (pkg/tracing/enrich_stability.go)
- [x] Console: sparkline panel and explainer modal (dashboards/observability/invocation_stability_panel.json, web/ui/components/InvStabilitySparkline.tsx)
- [x] Backfill helper: script to compute scores for 7 days of historical data (tools/backfill/invocation_stability_backfill.py)
- [x] Unit + integration tests; e2e UI smoke test
- [x] Docs: added explainer and troubleshooting guide (docs/observability/invocation_stability.md)

Commits summary: "initial score pipeline and unit tests"; "add span enrichment and attribute mapping"; "Console sparkline and explainer modal"; "backfill tool and docs"; "fix sparkline pixel alignment and tests".

High-level changed files: ["observability/metrics/invocation_stability.go", "pkg/tracing/enrich_stability.go", "web/ui/components/InvStabilitySparkline.tsx", "dashboards/observability/invocation_stability_panel.json", "tools/backfill/invocation_stability_backfill.py", "docs/observability/invocation_stability.md", "observability/metrics/tests/stability_test.go", "web/ui/__tests__/InvStabilitySparkline.test.tsx", "deploy/helm/values.observability.yaml", "scripts/ci/sparkline_lint.sh", "web/api/metrics_handlers.go"]

Testing and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky unit test in web/ui/__tests__/InvStabilitySparkline.test.tsx related to SVG rendering in the JSDOM environment. I updated the test to mock getBoundingClientRect and added a retry on CI. Final CI status: initial failure on unit tests -> fix in second commit -> full pipeline passed (unit/integration/e2e smoke). Perf: score compute added ~0.9ms median per-invocation on a light-weight pathway; we added the computation on the ingestion hot path only when samples are being collected (sampled-stability config default: 5%). Benchmarked with local load generator; cost impact negligible at default sampling.

Review thread (selected):
- Marcus Chen (review): "Nice existing metrics reuse; a few nits: 1) please avoid storing full contributor list in metric tags (cardinality risk) — store top3 only; 2) clarify normalization constants and make them configurable via config store."
- Aisha (author reply): "Good catch on cardinality; implementation stores only top3 contributors and uses bounded enums for contributor keys. Normalization constants moved to runtime config with defaults from ENG-8734."
- Lena Ortiz (review): "Can we include an endpoint in the metrics API that returns the scoring breakdown for a single invocation id? That would help programmatic triage."
- Aisha: "Added web/api/metrics_handlers.go#GetInvocationStability to return a small JSON blob (score + contributors) and guarded it behind observability.read scope. Included API schema in docs."
- Sven H (review): "Tests look good; one minor performance concern around serialization in backfill script."
- Aisha: "Addressed by streaming encoder in backfill commit."
- CI: "initial unit-test failure (sparkline svg) resolved by mocking getBoundingClientRect and retry on CI."

Edge cases and privacy: we avoid persisting raw prompt/token text; all scoring inputs are numeric aggregates (counts, rates, flags). Backfill operates on token-level aggregates only; no PII introduced. Access control: the new API endpoint is gated by observability.read and the Console component respects RBAC.

Operational notes:
- Config knobs: observability.stability.sampling_rate (default 0.05), observability.stability.weights.{latency,cost,cache,fallback,size} (defaults in docs), observability.stability.alert_tiers (maps score thresholds to alert severities).
- Alerts: this PR introduces two suggested SLO alert templates that map Stability < 40 to P2, 40-60 to P3, and <80 as a watch. Templates are in dashboards/alerts/stability_alert_templates.json. We left them disabled by default; customers can enable in Console.

Migration/rollout: The scoring is additive; metric names are new (invocation.stability_score, invocation.stability_top_contributors). Rollout plan: initial feature-gated rollout to 10% of accounts for 3 days (feature flag: observability.invocation_stability.enabled) then ramp to 100% if no regressions. Backfill can be run by SRE via tools/backfill/invocation_stability_backfill.py to populate dashboards for the past 7 days.

Risks: potential metric cardinality if contributor keys were unbounded (mitigated by top3 and bounded contributor enum), small CPU overhead at ingestion when sampling rate is high. Tested under load and added an autotune suggestion warning in Console when sampling rate > 20%.

Related work: complements token-cost and KV cache metrics (see ENG-9123 and recent dashboards). Linear: ENG-8734 tracks design and rollout checklist. SUP-1023 reported multiple noisy alerts that motivated this work.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main. Merge commit notes: "Add invocation stability score + Console explainer sparkline (ENG-8734)". Post-merge actions: created runbook entry in runbooks/observability/invocation_stability_runbook.md and scheduled a short docs webinar for the customer success team.
